cues.en: Now we have learned about recursion.
So we need to identify when to use the recursion and when to avoid it.
So first let's look at in which cases we can use the recursion.
Now if we can divide the problem into similar subproblems which is going to be the smaller subproblems.
In this case we need to use the recursion.
And we need to take into account that if we are fine with the extra overhead, in this case, we can
use it because the time and space complexity for recursive function is not efficient.
So that's why if you don't care about the time and space complexity, you can use the recursive solution.
And if you need a quick working solution instead of efficient one, you can use the recursion.
Because writing recursive functions is easier than the iterative ones when it comes to the very complex
method, and when we are using the tree traversal, usually we use the recursive functions, but it's
possible to do it with iterative functions as well.
So in our upcoming sections I'm going to show you both ways.
And the last point is that when we use the memoization in recursion, we have to use the recursive function.
So we are going to talk about this also in our upcoming sections.
Now when it comes to the when we avoid the recursion, if the time and space complexity matters for
us.
So if we need the efficient solution, we don't need to use the recursive solution, because in most
cases, recursive solutions are not efficient and recursion uses the more memory.
So for example, if you are writing an application which uses the embedded memory of the phones.
So if we use the recursive solutions, the application is not going to be efficient because it's going
to use the more memory in the phone.
That's why it's advisable to use the other solutions when the memory matters to us.
So it's not going to be memory efficient solution.
So with this we have come to the end of this section.
Hopefully everything is clear about recursion.
